findings.problem: JobWorkflow has no typestate enum - any combination of status, is_validated, is_sent is representable, including logically impossible states like validated-but-not-sent with status "new" and is_sent=true
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct states where the job lifecycle invariants are violated, such as is_sent=true while status remains "new", or is_validated=true with status "invalidated"
findings.fix: replace status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms with a single JobState enum (e.g., New, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }) so transitions are enforced by the type system

findings.problem: status: String allows arbitrary invalid strings like "sent", "SENT", "", "pending2", "null" that have no meaning in the domain
findings.failure_mode: pattern matching or string comparison on status cannot exhaustively cover all states; typos in status strings silently create unknown states instead of compile-time errors
findings.fix: replace String with a domain enum JobStatus { New, Validated, Sent } and expose it as an immutable field on the typestate

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are separate booleans that do not encode transition rules; the struct allows is_validated=false with is_sent=true (sent without validation)
findings.failure_mode: business logic can observe inconsistent lifecycle: mark_sent sets is_sent=true but never touches is_validated, leaving the struct in an arbitrary validated/sent combination with no invariant guarantee
findings.fix: collapse lifecycle booleans into a single typestate enum with explicit variants and transition methods; remove is_validated and is_sent fields entirely

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is decoupled from is_sent: bool - sent_at_epoch_ms can be Some(value) while is_sent=false, or None while is_sent=true
findings.failure_mode: consumers checking is_sent=true may expect a timestamp but find None; consumers checking sent_at_epoch_ms.is_some() may assume is_sent=true but it is not; the two fields are in a data race of truth
findings.fix: fold sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant of the typestate enum so the timestamp only exists when the job is in the Sent state, eliminating the decoupling

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain semantics - any empty string, whitespace, or malformed value is accepted as a valid job ID
findings.failure_mode: no validation at construction; ID collisions, empty-job lookups, and injection attacks are possible because the type provides no invariants on its content or length
findings.fix: introduce a non-zero JobId newtype with a smart constructor that validates the string (non-empty, bounded length) and returns a typed error, then use JobId in JobWorkflow

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts a fully-formed JobWorkflow directly and mutates status and is_sent in place - raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly and bypass all transition validation
findings.failure_mode: any caller with a JobWorkflow reference can call mark_sent even if the job is in an invalid predecessor state (e.g., never validated, or already marked sent), because there is no state-gated constructor or smart constructor at the boundary
findings.fix: add a fallible smart constructor JobWorkflow::new(...) that validates the initial state, replace mark_sent with a state-gated method like JobWorkflow::try_mark_sent(self) -> Result<Self, TransitionError>, and make all fields private behind the typestate

findings.problem: All fields of JobWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to mutate status, is_validated, and is_sent independently without any transition validation
findings.failure_mode: external code can set item.status = "anything"; item.is_validated = false; item.is_sent = true; all in one expression, creating impossible states without going through mark_sent or any transition method
findings.fix: make all fields private and provide only state-gated constructor and transition methods

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts any JobWorkflow and unconditionally sets status to "sent" and is_sent=true, with no check on is_validated or current status
findings.failure_mode: a job can be marked sent without ever being validated, bypassing the intended validation gate; calling mark_sent twice is silently idempotent, losing the ability to detect duplicate operations
findings.fix: gate the transition on the current state: require is_validated=true and is_sent=false before allowing mark_sent, returning Result<JobWorkflow, TransitionError> to make failures explicit

residual_risk: static review only; no commands run. JobWorkflow is a trivial struct but represents all canonical typestate violations: status-as-string, lifecycle booleans, decoupled Option data, raw-string IDs, no smart constructor, and a state-ungated mutation function. Without enum/typestate refactoring, the API is a footgun for invariant violations.
